golfista.mp3: I have made that shot 10,000 times. That day, I could feel my left hand on the club. I could feel where my shoulder was. I remember thinking, keep the arm slow, keep it straight, do not move the head. And I did all of it correctly. The ball went four meters past the hole. I have never missed that shot in practice, not once.
lab.mp3: A study from 2005. Two groups of students and the same math problems. One group worked in silence. The other group worked for money on camera with a partner who depended on them. The results surprised the researchers. The students with the best memory for numbers lost the most points. The other students did not change at all. The pressure did not take something from everybody. It took from the people who had the most to use.
palestra.mp3: there were about 60 people. I knew the material. I had the whole thing in my head an hour before. Then I started thinking about the man in the second row. The one who was not smiling. And about the time. And about the questions at the end. And whether the file would open. I got to slide 4 and I could not remember what came next. It was my own slide. I wrote it.
treinador.mp3: There are two of you, and you need different things. If your head leaves the task, you do not need more practice. You need practice with the pressure already in the room. And you need one small thing you always do first, the same thing, every time. If your head goes into your own hands, do the opposite. Give your attention something outside your body. Watch the ball, watch the person's face, not the arm.
